title: Tiered capacity buckets & emergency patch credits prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: validate a two-axis packaging prototype for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that reduces procurement friction while preserving upgrade safety and predictable unit economics. The prototype bundles: 1) Tiered 'capacity buckets' (monthly commit bands of inference credits + baseline license fee) and 2) A small emergency patch credit pool that customers can spend for out-of-band hotfix/upgrade operations without requiring a formal change order. We need to evaluate revenue uplift, sales cycle impact, support load during upgrades, and SQ (security questionnaire) answers alignment. This ticket coordinates PM, Sales, Legal, and Security to run a 3-month pilot with 6 existing prospects and 3 internal dev sandboxes.
background: Enterprise prospects report two procurement frictions: (a) unpredictable token consumption makes fixed license pricing risky and (b) emergency change orders for urgent security patches introduce long procurement delays. Past experiments focused on commit bands (see PM-7421/PM-32456) and reserve credits; this prototype attempts to: - introduce compact commit buckets (small/medium/large) tied to credit pools and a simple license multiplier, and - add a purchasable emergency patch credit pack (non-refundable, burnable for hotfix deploys or immediate rollback support). We must ensure the approach maps cleanly to our Dedicated and Private offerings and keeps auditability for SQ responses.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 capacity bucket SKUs (S/M/L) with license fee + monthly credit quantity and published unit economics
Document emergency patch credit SKU and allowed redemption rules; Legal sign-off on T&Cs for credits
Run 6 customer pilots with pricing proposals and capture win/loss reasons
Instrument console billing and per-route cost dashboards to report usage vs commit (dashboard link included)
Updated SQ template answers and a Security FAQ for emergency patch handling approved by Security
success_metrics: >10% uplift in deal close rate for pilot cohort vs baseline
Average sales cycle time reduced by 2+ weeks for pilot deals
<=1 support-engineer-day per pilot customer during upgrade windows
0 critical SQ blockers opened by pilot customers related to patch credits
tradeoffs_and_risks: Sales may prefer ad-hoc discounts over committing to standardized buckets; risk of increased discounting
Emergency patch credits introduce a liability on books and ambiguous SLAs if not tightly scoped
Complexity in billing instrumentation for hybrid commits (hosted vs on-prem metering)
Upsell friction: customers might under-commit to avoid overpaying, reducing expected revenue uplift
implementation_notes: Engineering will need a lightweight billing hook and API flag to mark 'emergency patch' operations so they consume credits. Console UI: show remaining bucket credits and emergency credit pool; add an admin flow to redeem emergency credits. Eng ticket ENG-7241 covers meter tagging and Dashboard query changes. Legal to draft credit T&Cs and an appendix for enterprise contracts. Security will run a short review focusing on audit trails and RBAC for emergency deploys.
